A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SPLITS! dataset and hypothesis-filtering framework. The complete main texts and appendices are readable, and corresponding equations, tables, and figures can be matched despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V2 reports original Reddit analyses, replications of linguistic phenomena, hypothesis-filtering results, and a 500-hypothesis human-rating study, including results in Appendices B and D.

after.justification: V3 retains those empirical results and adds human annotation audits, a Korean demographic-extraction failure case, and evaluation of literature-inspired hypotheses.

M1.justification: The seed-subreddit/group-ness construction, ColBERT and LLM topic filtering, BM25 retrieval, lift calculation, and BERT-based Triviality metric remain unchanged. Literature-conditioned generation supplies an additional validation set rather than changing the proposed filtering method.

E1.justification: The 9.7-million-post dataset, six retained demographics, 89 topics, and existing linguistic case studies remain. V3 adds a Korean demographic-construction failure scenario and a literature-derived evaluation set containing 132 lexica and 591 hypotheses from 11 sources. These extend evaluation coverage without replacing the central corpus.

E2.justification: V3 adds an explicit regex-only versus regex-plus-LLM comparison for self-identification validation (Table 9), absent from v2. The original prompt variants, case-study demographic comparisons, and unfiltered baseline in the efficiency table are retained.

E3.justification: V3 introduces several validation protocols: a 112-post self-identification audit, a 100-post topic audit, and a 44-item, four-choice literature-alignment test. Section 6.1 also changes the stated promising criterion from all three ratings being at least 3 to an average above 3, although Appendix D retains the original rule. This documents inconsistent settings, not evidence that the original experiment was rerun.

E4.justification: New analyses test the reliability of both LLM annotation stages, explain demographic extraction failure for Koreans, and assess Triviality against literature-inspired hypotheses and their source alignment. V3 also extends prompt analysis with lift summaries and replaces the illustrative surfaced hypotheses. These substantially broaden validation and failure analysis.

E5.justification: The lift–Triviality association changes from Pearson correlation, reported as 0.30, to Spearman correlation, reported as 0.32. This changes the statistical estimator. The original human-rating ICC, unexpectedness correlation, and case-study confidence-interval reporting remain; no additional repeated-run scheme is documented.

E6.justification: V3 newly reports self-identification F1 values of 0.698 for regex and 0.930 for regex plus LLM, topic-classification F1 of 0.96, mean Triviality of 0.585 versus 0.810 for literature-inspired versus ordinary hypotheses, and 42/44 correct source-alignment identifications. Korean failure results and prompt-wise lift summaries are also added. Original case-study values and the efficiency table remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions of group-ness, lift, and Triviality, together with the self-identification assumptions, are retained. Numbering the Triviality equation and expanding sociolinguistic motivation introduce no new formal result, derivation, or proof.

C1.justification: The contribution list now foregrounds a reusable sandbox-construction method, presenting SPLITS! as an instance and hypothesis filtering as an application. This modestly redefines the contribution emphasis; the substantive claims about the dataset, lexical filtering, and subsequent expert investigation remain.

C2.justification: V3 adds substantive qualifications concerning seed-community purity, amplification of group differences through sampling, LLM-generated hypothesis bias, and embedding-related Triviality failures. It interprets published findings as a proxy for interestingness and replaces the rural-economics discussion with a tentative religious-worldview interpretation of healthcare vocabulary. These substantially expand applicability boundaries and interpretation.

D1.justification: V3 supplies code, dataset, and demo links; exact group-ness thresholds for all six demographics; model identifiers and their roles beyond the previously specified topic-filtering model; and the literature-conditioned generation prompt. These materially improve access and reproducibility documentation without establishing changes to existing implementations. V2's explicit MIT-license statement is omitted.

R1.justification: Related work is substantially repositioned around variationist and third-wave sociolinguistics and automated social-science hypothesis research, adding works by Gumperz, Chambers, Eckert, Jaffe, Yang, Manning, and Peterson, among others. V3 also adds literature-validation sources and theological references while removing the earlier cross-science discovery, creativity, and dance-context citations.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work, and conclusion are extensively rewritten around the sandbox narrative. Dataset construction is divided into explicit stages, validation and application receive separate treatment, and existing case-study and generation explanations move into appendices. This is substantial narrative reorganization beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: V3 adds overview and dataset-construction diagrams, redraws the filtering diagram, simplifies the scatterplot legend, and consolidates existing case-study results in Table 1. It adds a literature-distribution figure and validation tables and replaces the illustrative hypothesis figure with a table. Many existing appendix plots are retained and relocated.

improvement.justification: Compared with v2, v3 provides direct human checks of dataset annotation, documents a concrete failure boundary, and improves access information, reproducibility details, and workflow explanation. These strengthen support and usability. The gain is tempered by small, single-annotator validation studies and new main-text/appendix inconsistencies, particularly the conflicting promising criteria attached to unchanged efficiency results.
